channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] France expects EU sanctions on 14 December over Iran’s refrigeration sabotage as Iran-linked hackers turn to physical attacks
item.description: France’s foreign minister said on 17 November he expects EU foreign ministers to agree sanctions on 14 December against the people behind October’s sabotage of supermarket refrigeration controllers, freezing their assets and barring travel, a day after EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas confirmed new Iran sanctions are being prepared. Paris blames the IRGC’s Shahid Kaveh unit for the attack on about 700 French sites, which French authorities say caused at least 15 fires, and has sought arrest warrants for three officers; Iran rejects the accusations. Health-ISAC warned on 16 November that settings were also changed at French blood-service sites, putting donor blood and therapies at risk. US and Israeli officials have told the Wall Street Journal that Iran-linked hackers also sabotaged equipment at small Midwest water stations and aboard two tankers. For OT defenders the lesson is plain: any internet-reachable controller is now a proven target. - Arab News, from AFP (17 Nov 2026, Barrot: EU decision expected 14 Dec); APA (18 Nov 2026, Barrot on France 5: sanctions within a month); dpa, via Yahoo News (16 Nov 2026, Kallas: EU sanctions in preparation); Asharq Al-Awsat and The New Arab (16 Nov 2026, French sanctions push); Health-ISAC (16 Nov 2026, cold-chain bulletin); Wall Street Journal (13 Nov 2026), via Newsmax wire on Yahoo News and Voice of Emirates; RFI via AOL (11 Nov 2026, Paris prosecutor’s warrant request); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French attribution and at least 15 fires); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Midnight Blue (Nov 2026, AK-SM 800A research); GBHackers (13 Nov 2026); NPR (9 Nov 2026, Iranian denial); Iran International (14 Nov 2026, IRGC response); Arab News, from AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement) - Barrot: EU sanctions within a month 17–18 Nov 2026; EU confirms sanctions in preparation, French sanctions push and Health-ISAC bulletin 16 Nov 2026; WSJ report 13 Nov 2026; BSI and CCB warnings 13 Nov 2026; warrant request 11 Nov 2026; French attribution 9 Nov 2026; IRGC rejects French findings 14 Nov 2026; October attack 11–12 Oct 2026; investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] CISA and FBI warn of an ongoing threat to internet-connected refrigeration as European supermarket attacks reach at least 11 countries
item.category: Incident — CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT joint warning (5 Nov 2026) and a second wave of refrigeration attacks across about 11 European countries (1–4 Nov); Belgium says its evidence points to Iran (12 Nov), no formal attribution
item.description: Hackers are tampering with internet-connected refrigeration controllers in European supermarkets, and on 5 November CISA and the FBI, with HHS, USDA and DOT, warned the threat is ongoing and also reaches healthcare, chemical, transport and cold-storage operations. Hundreds of French stores were hit in October; a second wave on 1–2 November reached about 11 countries, forcing units into continuous heating or defrost, and three French blood-service sites had settings changed with no blood lost. Sweden’s NCSC says victims at Coop and ICA stores mainly ran older systems from one manufacturer with weak passwords. Belgium’s interior minister said on 12 November that evidence points to Iran, short of formal attribution (see top story); a pro-Russian claim is unverified. Exposed Danfoss StoreView instances fell from 3,004 to 708 between 9 October and 5 November. Sekoia says the second wave used a non-public, unauthenticated flaw that renames the controller’s admin account. If a controller is reachable from the internet, treat it as at risk today. - TechCrunch (5 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI joint statement); SentinelOne Labs (3 Nov 2026, updated 4 Nov); Cybersecurity Dive (3 Nov 2026, updated with 4 Nov developments); Unit 42 (6 Nov 2026, exposure counts); Censys (6 Nov 2026, exposure analysis); BleepingComputer (5 Nov 2026); Nextgov (29 Oct 2026); Al Jazeera (4 Nov 2026); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012; The Cyber Express (6 Nov 2026, CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory summary); Industrial Cyber (6 Nov 2026); Help Net Security (6 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (6 Nov 2026, hardening guidance); The Hacker News (9 Nov 2026, exposure trend); eBuilder Security (11 Nov 2026, Swedish government and NCSC warning); Arab News/AFP (12 Nov 2026, Belgian statement); Sekoia TDR (10 Nov 2026, second-wave technique) - Attacks overnight 1–2 Nov 2026; Germany, Romania and UK confirmed 4 Nov 2026; CISA/FBI joint warning 5 Nov 2026; French attribution of the October attack 9 Nov 2026; Swedish government warning 10 Nov 2026; Belgian minister points to Iran 12 Nov 2026 — investigations ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — PHP2Shell plus Gaia root flaw CVE-2026-123039 used to backdoor Check Point gateways and wipe a VMware ESXi host (wave 1 from 30 Oct, Israel; wave 2 from 2 Nov, multiple countries); CVE-2026-123039 added to CISA KEV 13 Nov 2026
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw (CVE-2026-123039) to become root. They planted backdoors, pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper. The first wave hit Israeli organizations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries without destruction. Attribution is unconfirmed (tooling resembles China-nexus UNC5221). CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No OT victim is reported, but these firewalls often sit at the IT/OT boundary and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); BleepingComputer (Nov 2026) - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell attacks rooted about two dozen Palo Alto firewalls, and Siemens, Schneider and ABB now list grid-control, DCS and RTU products, several with no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell chained with a Linux kernel flaw to root exposed PAN-OS firewalls, 23–24 Oct; OT vendor advisories 28–30 Oct; Siemens adds metering gateways 16 Nov
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified that a suspected China-nexus actor chained the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials. Siemens (Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways), Schneider (a Foxboro DCS server) and ABB (Netcontrol RTUs, ASPECT gateways) now list affected products, several unfixed. None is reported exploited and no OT operator is named: treat it as an IT-to-OT boundary warning. - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026) and Infosecurity Magazine (30 Oct 2026), citing Dream; CISA KEV catalog (30 Oct 2026 release); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026, WTV676/WTV776 added; V1.2 29 Oct 2026), SSA-566512 V1.1 (28 Oct 2026), SSA-019113 and SSA-082556; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); ABB Netcontrol and Arctic advisories (30 Oct 2026), ASPECT advisory (29 Oct 2026) and APROL SA26P015 (23 Oct 2026); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-127 and VDE-2026-137 - Root compromises 23–24 Oct 2026, verified by Unit 42 29 Oct 2026; KEV additions 26 and 28 Oct 2026; Siemens, Schneider and ABB updates 28–30 Oct 2026; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] A Chilean solar-and-battery plant is still off the grid nearly three months after a cyberattack, and lawmakers want answers
item.category: Incident — cyberattack forced Chile’s 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its battery system off the grid (attack 26 Aug 2026, forced disconnection 27 Aug); still offline per the 14 Nov 2026 grid-coordinator report; congressional information requests filed 11 Nov 2026; no attribution
item.description: The 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant in Chile’s Tarapacá region, with a 98 MW / 312 MWh battery system in commissioning, has been off the national grid since the National Electric Coordinator triggered its disconnection protocol on 27 August after a reported cyberattack. Its 14 November report still lists both assets at zero availability. On 11 November a member of Congress asked whether the national cybersecurity agency was notified as the law requires and which control systems were hit; no answer by 16 November. The owner, entry route and affected systems are undisclosed. The lesson: a plant pulled off the grid for safety can stay dark for months if it cannot be restored with confidence (editorial assessment). - ESS News / pv magazine (17 Nov 2026, citing Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional records); T13 (16 Nov 2026, in Spanish); pv magazine Latin America (16 Nov 2026, congressional requests, in Spanish) - Ongoing — still offline per 14 Nov 2026 coordinator report; congressional requests 11 Nov 2026; reported 16–17 Nov 2026; attack 26 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Equinor says the cyberattack on its IT systems has been stopped after three days, as a second Norwegian energy firm reports an attempted attack
item.category: Incident — Cyberattack on certain IT systems at Norway’s Equinor, disclosed 17 Nov 2026 and declared stopped on 20 Nov 2026; production unaffected throughout; Skagerak Energi reported an attempted attack on 18 Nov 2026; no attribution
item.description: Equinor, Norway’s state-controlled energy company and the EU’s largest pipeline-gas supplier, said on 20 November that the cyberattack on certain IT systems it disclosed on 17 November has been stopped. Production ran normally throughout, and it has found no sign that data was stolen or altered. Equinor says the attack was not a self-spreading virus and did not appear aimed specifically at it; police and Norway’s National Security Authority, which raised the national cyber risk level to “high” on 27 October, are involved. A day after Equinor’s first report, utility Skagerak Energi reported an attempted attack with operations unaffected. Neither has disclosed the entry route or attacker, and nothing points to OT. Two incidents at Norwegian energy firms in one week are reason to check IT-to-OT boundaries now (editorial assessment). - Rigzone (20 Nov 2026, attack stopped; Skagerak Energi attempted attack); Riviera Maritime Media (20 Nov 2026, timeline of Equinor updates and NSM risk level); Equinor statements (17–20 Nov 2026); Reuters (19 Nov 2026, attack still ongoing); The Record (18 Nov 2026) - Disclosed 17 Nov 2026; declared stopped 20 Nov 2026; Skagerak attempt reported 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Illinois investigates an apparent cyberattack attempt on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River
item.category: Incident — Attempted cyberattack on the state-run Algonquin Dam, Fox River, Illinois (16 Nov 2026; disclosed by IDNR 20 Nov 2026); dam kept secure and operating; CISA and state agencies investigating; no attribution
item.description: The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said on 20 November that it detected an apparent attempted cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam, about 45 miles northwest of Chicago, on 16 November. Staff blocked the unauthorised access at once, and the dam stayed secure and fully operational. IDNR has not said which system was targeted or whether gate controls were reachable. Illinois State Police, state agencies and CISA are investigating; no link to other attacks and no group has been named. For dam and flood-control owners, it is a prompt to check who can reach gate and spillway controls remotely (editorial assessment). - CBS Chicago (20 Nov 2026); ABC7 Chicago (20–21 Nov 2026); BNO News (21 Nov 2026); all citing the Illinois Department of Natural Resources - Attempt 16 Nov 2026; disclosed 20 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [High] Ransomware halts smart-meter production and shipments at Japan’s Osaki Electric
item.category: Incident — Ransomware at Japanese smart-meter maker Osaki Electric (confirmed 17 Nov 2026); production and shipments suspended at its Saitama centre and group plants (reported 18 Nov 2026); no group named
item.description: Osaki Electric, a Japanese smart-meter maker, said ransomware encrypted data on its servers on 17 November. It cut its systems off from outside networks and suspended production and shipments at its Saitama R&D and manufacturing centre and at group companies Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech; NHK reported the production-management system was among those knocked out. On 20 November the company said the intruder most likely got in on 15 November through a VPN device, by password guessing against an account without multi-factor authentication; some virtual servers were encrypted and technical information believed to be its own was posted online. No group has claimed it, and nothing suggests field meters or electricity supply are affected. For utilities, the risk is supply-chain: delayed meter rollouts, and how suppliers protect the systems that build and sign their devices (editorial assessment). - Osaki Electric announcements, via TipRanks (17 Nov 2026; updated 18 and 20 Nov 2026, entry route and data leak); NHK (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese); Kyodo, via Yahoo! Japan News and Tokyo Shimbun (18 Nov 2026, in Japanese) - Intrusion estimated 15 Nov 2026; attack confirmed 17 Nov 2026; entry route disclosed 20 Nov 2026; no production restart reported

item.title: [High] Cyberattack on Brazil’s Santos port authority forces manual workarounds at Latin America’s busiest port
item.category: Incident — Cyberattack on the Santos Port Authority (APS), Brazil; systems down from 6 Nov 2026, attack confirmed 10 Nov; port security raised to level 2 of 3 (8 Nov); core systems in final tests 16 Nov 2026; about 70% of backups recovered; Federal Police inquiry opened 10 Nov; no attribution
item.description: The Port of Santos authority, which runs Brazil’s largest port, lost its IT systems on 6 November and on 10 November confirmed a cyberattack. Access-control systems and digital tools for coordinating port operations went down, delaying vessel, truck and train procedures and forcing some checks, such as matching ship dimensions to berths, to be done by hand. The port’s protection level was raised to 2 of 3 on 8 November. By 16 November main internal systems were in final tests and about 70% of affected file backups were recovered; ship movements and landside access continued throughout. Brazil’s Federal Police are investigating; the attacker, entry route and any data theft are undisclosed. For port operators, access control and berth planning need a tested manual fallback (editorial assessment). - The Rio Times (16 Nov 2026, status update citing the Santos Port Authority); DatamarNews (10 Nov 2026, updated 11 Nov, citing A Tribuna); CyberDelegate (17 Nov 2026, citing Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil and Agência Brasil); Interlira Reports (17 Nov 2026) - Outage from 6 Nov 2026; security level raised 8 Nov 2026; attack confirmed 10 Nov 2026; core systems in final tests and ~70% of backups recovered 16–17 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US water, energy and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
item.category: Government threat assessment — DHS Secretary’s written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee (18 Nov 2026); DNI and DHS tell the same hearing recent US outages were not cyberattacks
item.description: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localized, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems, but warned that weak systems and poor cyber hygiene could have devastating consequences. At the same hearing the Director of National Intelligence and DHS said they found no evidence that hackers caused last week’s Microsoft 365 outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop or other recent disruptions, which officials tie to software defects and upgrade failures. Separately, AttackIQ research released on 17 November describes Iranian groups handing network access to one another, with long-running espionage access later passed to teams pursuing destructive goals, sometimes disguised as ransomware or hacktivism, often reaching targets through contractors and suppliers. For OT owners, the official US view now matches France’s: Iran is going after the weakest exposed controllers. - Jerusalem Post (18 Nov 2026, Mullin written testimony); Report.az (18 Nov 2026); Bloomberg (18 Nov 2026); Federal News Network (18 Nov 2026, outages not a coordinated attack); Washington Examiner (18 Nov 2026, hearing); AttackIQ “Weighing Cyber Power”, via Water Online (17 Nov 2026) - Testimony and hearing 18 Nov 2026; AttackIQ research 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware attacks on industrial organizations in Q3, up 11%, and found no case of an operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis for Q3 2026 (published 16 Nov 2026), covering July–September; Check Point October 2026 statistics (12 Nov 2026) for comparison
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organizations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, while the number of brands claiming industrial victims jumped from 70 to 99. Manufacturing took 69% of cases, followed by the ICS ecosystem of integrators, engineering firms and equipment makers (116) and transport and logistics (105); oil and gas logged 47. Qilin and The Gentlemen drove 29% of the total. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: production stopped because the IT, ERP and virtualization layers plants rely on went down, as when Fairlife reportedly halted all four of its US plants for about 11 days. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. Check Point separately counted a record 1,063 claimed victims across all sectors in October. - Dragos (16 Nov 2026); Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026); Check Point Research October 2026 statistics, via iTWire (12 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [High] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) exploited as a zero-day for more than two months by a suspected China-linked group, per Mandiant; Broadcom fix released 19 Nov 2026; no public fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported the bug, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221, also called Warp Panda) exploited it for more than two months beforehand. In the incidents Mandiant investigated, the group got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, moved to Linux appliances, attacked vCenter in early September with a custom tool called Bonesaw, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, created an SSO admin account, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. No victims or sectors are named. Many plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom, Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant and Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; exploited from at least early Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), clustered Expressway Core/Edge; exploited after a public PoC (reported by F6); added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; fixed in X15.5.20
item.description: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organization, moved to two more cluster nodes inside the network, and gained root. From there they ran Python scripts, which F6 says show signs of AI-assisted writing, to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to search GitLab for credentials. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 20 November alongside the vCenter zero-day. Cisco disclosed and fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No OT victim is reported, but Expressway is a perimeter gateway that often bridges outside callers into internal networks, so an exposed, unpatched cluster is a foothold close to plant-side systems (editorial assessment). - Security Affairs (21 Nov 2026, CISA KEV additions of 20 Nov); SecurityWeek (Nov 2026, citing F6); Security Affairs (20 Nov 2026, F6 findings) - Added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 18–20 Nov 2026; patched 21 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Hackers probe 14 newly disclosed flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers, five of which will never be fixed
item.category: Advisory — 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland (Dixell) XWEB EVO refrigeration supervisors disclosed by VulnCheck; CVE records published 12 Nov 2026 (incl. CVE-2026-124010, CVE-2026-124014); exploitation attempts seen within hours; five flaws will not be fixed
item.description: VulnCheck has disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland’s XWEB EVO, the Dixell supervisory system that runs supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, each of which gave its researcher root on test units. Nine affect only firmware built before a 2021 rewrite and include unauthenticated command execution and a hard-coded admin password. The other five reach the latest firmware: the daily admin password is derived from the device’s MAC address and the date, and the MAC address is visible without logging in, so an attacker can compute the password, turn on SSH and log in as root. VulnCheck’s sensors saw exploitation attempts against two older-firmware flaws within two hours of the 12 November CVE publication; it calls the sources opportunistic scanners, not the state campaign in France. Copeland ended XWEB EVO support on 16 March 2026 and will not fix the five current-firmware flaws; nearly 2,000 units are reachable from the internet. CyberScoop adds that XBOW honeypots posing as these controllers drew hundreds of requests and login attempts within a day, and someone changed the temperature on one simulated freezer. - SecurityWeek (16 Nov 2026, VulnCheck research and exploitation telemetry; Copeland end-of-life notice); CyberScoop (13 Nov 2026, XBOW honeypot findings; Copeland statement); CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 - CVE records published 12 Nov 2026; probing 12–13 Nov 2026; reported 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Six unpatched pre-login flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers prompt Belgian, German and Irish warnings to pull them off the internet
item.category: Advisory — Six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A (firmware up to 5.3.2), disclosed by Midnight Blue; Belgian CCB and German BSI warnings (13 Nov 2026), joined by Ireland’s NCSC; CVEs pending; no exploitation of these flaws reported
item.description: Amsterdam consultancy Midnight Blue has disclosed six stack buffer overflows in Danfoss AK-SM 800A system managers, the store-level controllers that run supermarket and cold-storage refrigeration, that allow remote code execution without logging in; one works even with “strict” session control turned on. All firmware up to 5.3.2 is affected and CVEs are still pending. The BSI says the 5.4.0 package released this month is not affected, but Midnight Blue says 5.4.0 predates its research and does not fix these bugs, so treat 5.4.0 as unconfirmed until Danfoss says otherwise. The researchers say an attacker could plant code that survives a factory reset or firmware update, or brick units, because the device does not appear to use secure boot; that is a stated possibility, not a demonstrated one. Belgium’s CCB and Germany’s BSI (13 November) and Ireland’s NCSC have all told operators that firmware updates, password changes and strict mode are not enough for internet-exposed units. Danfoss had published no advisory or fix date as of 16 November. No exploitation of these six flaws is reported. - Midnight Blue (Nov 2026); The Hacker News (16 Nov 2026, CCB, BSI and Irish NCSC warnings; Danfoss status); Bytes Europe (13 Nov 2026, CCB warning); Cyber Press (13 Nov 2026); Insurance Journal, from Reuters (13 Nov 2026, BSI warning); Filstalexpress (13 Nov 2026, BSI firmware details) - Status re-checked 16 Nov 2026 (no Danfoss fix); CCB and BSI warnings 13 Nov 2026; research published Nov 2026

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after attackers planted miners on servers already running Hotfix 2
item.category: Active exploitation — N-able N-central: 4EverAble2Shell exploited to plant miners (13 Nov 2026); N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and removes the Legacy API (16–17 Nov 2026); separate breach of N-able’s hosted Mail Assure/SpamExperts cloud disclosed 20 Nov 2026
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November, which it calls a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, missing authorization checks, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and it removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. On-premises servers need the upgrade now; hosted servers update automatically, but every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes, which N-able warns can otherwise be impersonated. The fix follows Huntback’s 13 November finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them on Hotfix 2. Remote control and Intune integration stay blocked for now. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, forcing it to take the management portal and APIs offline; it says mail flow continued, it has found no access to customer data, and the breach is unrelated to N-central. Many integrators manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools, and a miner today can be a hands-on intruder tomorrow (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (20 Nov 2026, Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach); The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback and Previdian); The Hacker News (12 Nov 2026, new chains); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Tenable (10 Nov 2026) - Mail Assure breach disclosed 20 Nov 2026; Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026; Able2Shell disclosed 9 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK “Java4Shell” memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026); exploitation attempts seen 18–19 Nov 2026; Siemens SSA-272816 lists three Industrial Edge Management products
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, started within two days of its 17 November disclosure. GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November and Previdian logged nine attempts from six addresses; none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups, each with a tailored chain. For OT teams the key item is Siemens advisory SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until they are patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, WatchTowr, Cloudflare, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert) - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Comments close 30 November on NIST’s draft rewrite of its OT security guide, which adds water, food, rail, maritime and building-automation coverage
item.category: Guidance — NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 4 draft (released 21 Sep 2026); public comments close 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST’s draft Revision 4 of SP 800-82, the US government’s main guide to operational technology security, is open for public comment until 30 November 2026. The draft reorganises the guide around Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with risk management now led by the Govern function, and adds sector material for building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels, and industrial IoT connected to cloud services. It also expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and detection, protecting system-management functions, and applying zero-trust principles. Many regulators, insurers and auditors use 800-82 as a reference, so its final wording can shape what operators are asked to show; the comment window is the chance for practitioners to flag guidance that would not work on a plant floor. - NIST CSRC, SP 800-82 Rev. 4 initial public draft (21 Sep 2026); SecurityWeek (24 Sep 2026) - Forward-looking: public comments close 30 Nov 2026
